turns.prompt_text: What's the difference between USB types
turns.response_html:
Understanding USB types can be a bit of a headache because the industry uses two different ways to categorize them: the physical shape of the connector and the data transfer speed (the "standards").

To make sense of it, it helps to think of the connector as the "shape of the pipe" and the standard as the "amount of water flowing through it."

1. Physical Connectors (The Shapes)

These are the physical ends of the cable you actually see and plug in.

  • USB-A: The classic rectangular connector found on almost every computer and wall charger. It only plugs in one way (usually the third try).
  • USB-B: A square-ish connector often used for large peripherals like printers and scanners.
  • Micro-USB: Once the standard for older Android phones and Kindle readers. It’s small and tapered on one side.
  • USB-C: The modern standard. It is symmetrical, reversible, and can handle significantly more power and data than its predecessors.

2. Transfer Standards (The Speed)

This determines how fast a file moves from your phone to your laptop. Note that a USB-C cable could be slow (USB 2.0) or incredibly fast (USB4), depending on its internal wiring.

StandardMax Transfer SpeedCommon Use Case
USB 2.0480 MbpsKeyboards, mice, and basic charging.
USB 3.0 / 3.15–10 GbpsExternal hard drives and high-speed data.
USB 3.220 GbpsHigh-performance SSDs.
USB440–80+ GbpsPro-level docking stations and high-res displays.

3. Power Delivery (Charging)

While older USB types could only provide enough juice for small electronics, USB-C with Power Delivery (USB-PD) can negotiate power levels. This allows a single cable to charge anything from a tiny pair of earbuds to a high-powered gaming laptop.

A Note on "Thunderbolt"

You will often see Thunderbolt (3 or 4) associated with USB-C. Thunderbolt uses the USB-C shape but is a premium technology developed by Intel. It generally offers the fastest possible speeds and the ability to "daisy-chain" multiple 4K monitors together.
